CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFSERVLET

NEW IN KOLDFUSION 4.5

CFSERVLET hands the request to a Java servlet running on an Allair JRun server and includes the servlet's output in the page, or stores it in a variable. KoldFusion cannot reach a JRun engine, so the tag always raises an Application error; catch it with CFTRY.

Category

Extensibility

Syntax

<CFSERVLET CODE="class_name_of_servlet"
    JRUNPROXY="proxy_server"
    TIMEOUT="seconds"
    WRITEOUTPUT="Yes/No"
    DEBUG="Yes/No">
  <CFSERVLETPARAM ...>
</CFSERVLET>

Attributes

CODE
Required. Class name of the servlet to run.
JRUNPROXY
Optional. Host and port of the JRun proxy, for example "127.0.0.1:8081".
TIMEOUT
Optional. Seconds to wait for the servlet.
WRITEOUTPUT
Optional, default "Yes". "Yes" writes the servlet's response into the page; "No" stores it in CFSERVLET.Output instead.
DEBUG
Optional, default "No". "Yes" writes extra information about the call.

Usage

Parameters are passed with CFSERVLETPARAM tags in the body. In ColdFusion the servlet's status and headers come back in the CFSERVLET structure.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFTRY>
  <CFSERVLET CODE="HelloWorldServlet" WRITEOUTPUT="Yes" TIMEOUT="10">
    <CFSERVLETPARAM NAME="greeting" VALUE="Hello from KoldFusion">
  </CFSERVLET>
  <CFCATCH TYPE="Application">
    <CFOUTPUT>
    <TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
    <TR BGCOLOR="##FFCCCC"><TH COLSPAN=2>The servlet could not run</TH></TR>
    <TR><TD>Message</TD><TD>#CFCATCH.Message#</TD></TR>
    <TR><TD>Detail</TD><TD>#CFCATCH.Detail#</TD></TR>
    </TABLE>
    </CFOUTPUT>
  </CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>

See also

CFSERVLETPARAM, CFOBJECT, CFHTTP, CFTRY
